| `city-ward` | City Council District | political | Polygon (dispatched, 2 cities) | **MICHIGAN'S FIRST DISPATCHED CONCEPT, AND ITS FIRST ALIAS SHIM.** Detroit shipped alone as `detroit-council` on 2026-09-05; Grand Rapids arrived the same day as the second city, so §3.0 converted the concept rather than adding a second near-identical layer — the expansion invariant says coverage changes which ENTRIES exist, never which LAYERS do. `registerCountyLayer` is ported from Iowa (a THIRD copy of shared code, recorded as a debt in `mi/WATCH.md`), keyed by CITY, and each entry brings its own card because the two cities are not alike: Detroit runs seven districts of ONE member with two at-large colleagues and no mayor, Grand Rapids three wards of TWO commissioners with a mayor and a seat the city does not publish. `CONSOLIDATED_LAYER_ALIASES` keeps every shipped `detroit-council` permalink working. **GRAND RAPIDS'S REAL QUESTION WAS AGE, AND MEASUREMENT ANSWERED IT**: its ward geometry was last edited 2018-01-24 while the item description claims currency, and Michigan's own 2026 precinct layer — which carries a WARD column, 20/20/19 over 59 precincts — dissolves to the same three lines on 99.575% of 4,000 points. Two independent publishers, one 2018 and one built for 2026, so 2018 means UNCHANGED. That agreement is a GATE. **THE ORG HOLDS EIGHT WARD SERVICES, NOT THE TWO THIS PR FIRST CLAIMED** — that count came off a search capped at the first 100 of its 681 feature services. Swept in full: three are 100.000% identical to what ships, one differs only at the perimeter, and three are SINGLE wards agreeing with their own shipped ward. No newer plan exists anywhere, so the currency finding stands and only the count was wrong. Balance 3.60% worst on Census 2020. **THE POPULATION IDENTITY IS NOT EXACT HERE AND IS NOT CLAIMED TO BE**, unlike Detroit's: 21 of 2,883 blocks sit on one side of the ward outline and the other side of the Census place outline (+66 against 198,917), two digitisations of one city edge, so the builder bounds it rather than asserting zero. Simplification is 50%, NOT the siblings' 20-25%: mapshaper's percentage is a share of the SOURCE vertex count, and on a three-feature layer 20% falls to 98.95% agreement, below the fleet floor — the floor was never the thing to move. Detroit's half is unchanged: **THE FIRST CITY TIER, and a case where four of the publisher's own services compete and the NAMES do not settle it.** Detroit's ArcGIS org carries `Council_Districts` titled "Current" (live since 2016), `city_council_districts_2026` (what ships), `city_council_districts_2013` — CREATED in December 2025, which is what archiving the old plan looks like — and `NewDistrictBoundariesOption6`, which reads like a rejected draft and **is not one**: measured 2026-09-05 it puts 99.575% of 4,000 points in the same district as the shipped service, with the residual at the city's outer edge and vertex counts 20-40% different per district against bounding boxes agreeing to ~100 m — the same lines REDIGITISED. It is the witness that names the dates, its own description reading "as adopted in February 2024". **THE PLAN'S DATES COME FROM THE SHIPPED SERVICE'S OWN `description` AND WERE MISSING FROM THE FIRST BUILD ENTIRELY**: adopted by the Council 2024-02-06, in effect 2026-01-01, both stated by the city on the data. ("2026-01-06", cited in the first build as the day the service was updated in place, is the AGO ITEM's `modified` timestamp; the service's `dataLastEditDate` is 2026-08-26.) Decided by MEASUREMENT and gated both ways: "Current" carries geometry identical to the 2026 service and different from the 2013 one, and on Census 2020 blocks the shipped plan runs 87,393–94,820 against a 91,302 ideal (worst **4.28%**) where the archive runs 78,966–100,623 (**13.51%**) — a plan drawn on 2010, seen from 2020. The build refuses if the archive ever balances too, because then the test has stopped discriminating. **THE SEVEN DISTRICTS SUM TO 639,111, DETROIT'S CENSUS 2020 POPULATION EXACTLY**, which is the tiling proof and is asserted rather than reported — and it is also why `coverage` is the layer's own tiling with no separate city outline: their union IS the city. Detroit's two AT-LARGE council seats correctly have no geometry | **ALL NINE MEMBERS, THROUGH THE FLEET'S OWN ARCHIVE RUNG — WHICH THIS LAYER SHIPPED WITHOUT TRYING.** The first version named nobody and said five routes were shut; two of those measurements were false. `data.detroitmi.gov` was called challenged when it answers **HTTP 200 with a readable robots.txt** — a verdict from grepping a 68 KB page for the word "challenge" and finding one hit WHILE THE STATUS CODE SAID 200. And the Internet Archive rung, in weekly use for Kendall and McHenry since 2026-07, was never attempted; it answers with all nine members, their districts and their roles. **A ROUTE NOT WALKED IS NOT A ROUTE MEASURED.** What survived: detroitmi.gov and mvic.sos.state.mi.us DO carry a genuine Cloudflare managed challenge on the plain AND the client-hints rung (the one that unblocked Kendall), so there is deliberately no headless rung here — a rung whose job is to wait out a challenge is the thing the rule is about. **LEGISTAR IS STILL THE SHARP ONE**: abandoned 2017-12-31 and its OfficeRecordTitle read "Council Member" with NO district even while maintained, where Milwaukee's reads "3rd District" — TEST A VENDOR BY CONTENT PER CITY. Seven members ride the polygons; the two AT-LARGE ship in a `citywide` block under their own heading (the Des Moines shape), and the card states which day's archived copy it read, refusing one over 45 days old. NO PER-MEMBER phone or e-mail anywhere on either surface, measured — but the BODY's own office IS published once (City Council Office, 2 Woodward Ave. Suite 1340, (313) 224-3443) and ships on the card under the switchboard rule; a first draft said the page carried no contact at all, which was true of its LINKS and false of its text. Gap `detroit-council-contact`, with NO ask drafted and the reason recorded: the city publishes no e-mail address to send one to. **GRAND RAPIDS NAMES SIX OF SEVEN AND THE CARD SAYS SO**: the city states its own arithmetic ("the Mayor and six Commissioners… the residents of each Ward directly elect two commissioners") and publishes ONE Ward 1 commissioner where Wards 2 and 3 have two — the Alexander `seats` machinery, used here for the first time on a DISTRICTED body. **THE SEVENTH SEAT IS A STATED VACANCY AND THIS PR FIRST SAID IT WAS NOT**: "no vacancy stated anywhere" was a measurement of ONE PAGE, and the city's own news post of 2026-04-17 states the vacancy "was created following the resignation of former Commissioner Drew Robbins". ONE PAGE IS NOT THE CITY — the same error that once called Detroit's open-data portal blocked. The card names the vacancy and its cause and says nothing about how it was resolved, because no city source does. The departed commissioner's own page still answers 200 and is still in the sitemap, so a scraper walking sitemap entries would ship him as sitting. Each member's own page gives their ward, e-mail and direct phone; **the e-mail domain is `grcity.us` and NOT the website's**, so a scraper keyed to the site's own hostname finds none, and 616.456.3000 is on every page and is the switchboard, DETECTED rather than hardcoded. Two parse traps, both caught by gates rather than by eye: the listing's role labels sit beside an anchor that is not their own (the Franklin grid trap — pairing role to link put Ward 1 on a Ward 3 member), and the role is a standalone line on only three of the six pages |
| `county-commissioner` | County Commissioner District | political | Polygon | **THE FLAGSHIP, and the reason Michigan was chosen as the sixth state.** Pre-built from the Michigan Bureau of Elections' statewide compilation of the plans county apportionment commissions file under MCL 46.401-46.405 — 619 districts, all 83 counties, one query. Licence stated outright on the AGO dataset item ("a public record … no restrictions on the use, reproduction, or distribution"); the Hub SITE item's CC-BY-SA is a different item and its share-alike is NOT inherited. Named 2021 (adoption), labelled 2022 by the state's own viewer (first election under it), feature class `CCD_2022_Edit` — three names, ONE layer, and no successor exists (all 294 `michigan_admin` items enumerated; the state's current Election District Viewer still wires this endpoint). Every Michigan county elects by single-member district, so a polygon is honest everywhere with no at-large carve-out | — **GEOMETRY ONLY, BY MEASUREMENT.** The source ships a Commissioner and Party on all 619 polygons and the builder DROPS them. The item's own description says they were "derived from the canvased November 2024 election results", so the column lists certified WINNERS, not officeholders — which is exactly why it is 100% filled, since a winners list is complete by construction and can never be blank. Measured 2026-09-03 over 12 counties read district-by-district against their own board pages (123 districts) plus ~40 more adversarially: 93.5% named the right person, and EVERY miss ran the same direction (layer = 2024 winner, county = their replacement). Wayne D5 still names Irma Clark-Coleman, who died 10 June 2025; four further rows misspell a real surname. `build_mi_commissioner_districts.py` refuses to write if those columns ever reach `data/app/`. Gap `mi-commissioner-roster`; the honest route is county-by-county, and 10 of the 12 sampled counties publish a readable board page |
| `school-district-unified` | School District (Unified) | schools | Polygon | LIVE TIGERweb School L0 (`STATE='26'`, 514 districts) through `tigerStatewideLoader` — no builder, no committed `data/app` file, so a vintage roll reaches it on its own. **The helper it uses was DELETED at go-live and re-added here on purpose**: Michigan inherited it unused from Iowa, and `build_privacy_page.py` measures point-query layers by counting `loadArcGISPointGeoJSON` call sites, so the dead wrapper made the published privacy page claim a Michigan layer sent the reader's exact point to a government server when none did. The note left in its place said to re-add it with the first live layer that needs it | — (identity only). Gap `mi-school-board-members`: Michigan school boards are elected (MCL 380.11a et seq.) and no statewide roster exists — TIGERweb's fields are geographic plus grade range, so unlike the commissioner layer there is no stale name here to reject. The Dept. of Education's Educational Entity Master is an entity/administrator directory, not a board roster; the school-boards association is membership-facing |
| `school-district-elementary` | School District (Elementary) | schools | Polygon | LIVE TIGERweb School L2 (27 districts). **NOT OPTIONAL, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY**: these are GAP-FILLS, not overlays — at all 27 TIGER interior points the unified layer returns nothing, and at every unified district's interior point this layer returns nothing, so shipping unified alone would answer "no school district" to everyone living in one of the 27. Both cards carry the other's name in their `emptyNote`, which was itself found by rendering the pair at Bois Blanc: the unified card had been falling through to the engine's generic "isn't inside any district", reading like a failed lookup rather than the answer it is. **THE PROBE HAS A TRAP worth carrying to any instance**: run against TIGER's `CENTLAT/CENTLON` (the mathematical centroid, which for a non-convex polygon can sit outside its own shape) it reports one false overlap; against `INTPTLAT/INTPTLON`, the interior point TIGER guarantees is inside, it is 27 of 27 clean. **USE `INTPT*`, NEVER `CENT*`** | — (identity only), same gap `mi-school-board-members` |
| `county-subdivision` | Township or City | geography | Bespoke | LIVE TIGERweb Places/CouSub L1 (1,581 records). `subOf: "county"`, and the containment is IN THE KEY rather than assumed — TIGER's GEOID is state + county + subdivision. Measured 2026-09-04: 1,122 general-law townships (LSADC 44) + 118 CHARTER townships (49) + 301 city placeholder records (25, FUNCSTAT F) for 281 distinct cities, 18 of which cross a county line + 40 "not defined" records measuring 0 m² of land and 91,090 km² of water, i.e. the Great Lakes. **THE CHARTER/GENERAL-LAW DISTINCTION COSTS NO SECOND SOURCE**: it is read from what TIGER's own NAME carries beyond BASENAME ("Ypsilanti" + " charter township"), the WI/IA technique, so the type row can never disagree with the name printed above it — the four LSADC values yield exactly four suffixes across 1,581 of 1,581 | — (identity only). Gap `mi-township-officers`: 1,240 township boards (supervisor, clerk, treasurer, trustees — MCL 41.61; MCL 42.3 for charter townships), no statewide roster. The card NAMES THE OFFICE and says plainly it does not know who holds it |
| `municipality` | City or Village | geography | Bespoke | LIVE TIGERweb Places L4 (533 places: 280 cities C5 + 1 C6 + 252 villages C1). **THIS IS THE LAYER PAIR MICHIGAN'S STRUCTURE TURNS ON, and it differs from BOTH siblings**: a Michigan CITY is independent of any township, while a VILLAGE remains part of one — so a village resident has two general-purpose local governments and a city resident has one. Measured 2026-09-04 across ALL 252 villages at their TIGER interior points: every one lands inside a township (235 general-law, 17 charter), zero exceptions, and the Census's own class codes agree (every village is C1, "does not serve as a county subdivision equivalent"). Each card names the other, so the duplication a reader sees at a village is explained rather than discovered. Contrast Iowa (cities only, no village class) and Wisconsin (cities AND villages are themselves subdivisions) | — (identity only). Gap `mi-municipal-officeholders`. **NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH IOWA**: Iowa's League of Cities publishes a per-city row carrying the OFFICE's phone and website for 927 of 939, which is why Iowa's card can reach the city while naming nobody; nothing equivalent was found for Michigan, so this card carries neither person nor phone |
| `precinct` | Precinct | political | Polygon | PRE-BUILT from the Bureau of Elections' own **2026 Voting Precincts** (AGO item `c349bc2bb6c2468594d341a09f520ea8`), 3,895 precincts across all 83 counties, paged and Visvalingam-simplified by `mi/scripts/build_mi_precincts.py` (2,000-point gate). **IT NEARLY SHIPPED THE 2024 MAP**: the state's `OpenData/boundaries` MapServer publishes a layer per cycle and its newest is 2024 (layer 9), so enumerating that MapServer gives a complete answer from an incomplete place to look — the 2026 map is on the AGO ORG, a different host, and Michigan consolidated 4,340 -> 3,895 between cycles, so 2024 was 445 precincts wrong. The org query costs one request and belongs BEFORE any MapServer's layer list. Four items serve the 2026 map; the builder pins the CURATED one (title, licence, caveat description, full field names) and gates on the one the state's own viewer wires (`VotingPrecincts2026_051926_gdb`, truncated field names, empty description) reporting the same count. **THE MCD JOIN IS EXACT**: all 1,530 distinct `"26"`+county+MCD keys resolve against the Census MCD fabric this instance ships, the same 1,530 on both cycles because the consolidation happened WITHIN municipalities | — **NO OFFICEHOLDER** (a precinct elects nobody; it is the unit a ballot is counted in) **AND NO POLLING PLACE, which here is a fact about the source rather than a decision**: the layer carries no polling field at all, so unlike `ia/`'s builder there is nothing to decline. The card carries registered voters LABELLED WITH THEIR CYCLE and the state's own caveat in substance — validation "done by most, but not all" jurisdictions, the data "only as good as the information received from the local election official" — then points a reader at their clerk. `Tabulator_Voter_Assist` is deliberately never fetched: it moves on a different clock from the boundary, and a field never fetched cannot be added by a later edit that forgets why |
| `zip-code` | ZIP Code | geography | Polygon | LIVE TIGERweb ZCTA (layer 11), no builder and no `data/app` file. **THE ONE TIGERweb LAYER HERE THAT CANNOT USE `STATE='26'`** — ZCTAs cross state lines and carry no STATE field — so it is fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE, and **the envelope must be Esri's own `{xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax}`**: passing this instance's `{minLng,...}` `METRO_BBOX` makes TIGERweb answer **HTTP 200 with a JSON error envelope and zero features**, the exact trap `loadTigerLayer`'s guard exists for. That is not hypothetical — **`ia/` shipped that bug and this change fixes it**, its overlay having silently never drawn while its card kept working (a point query sends a point, not an envelope). `il/`, `wi/` and `ca/` each declare their own correctly-shaped envelope constant; Iowa's port reused `METRO_BBOX` and inherited the wrong key names. **NEIGHBOURING STATES' ZIPS ARE IN THE OVERLAY AND NO RECTANGLE FIXES IT**: Michigan's box returns 2,000 ZCTAs of which 1,010 sit east of -87.60, because it runs west across Lake Michigan, and even the clipped box catches Chicago's 60628 | — **no officeholder, and none is missing**: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card states what the boundary actually IS — a Census areal approximation of USPS delivery routes, not a postal boundary — rather than letting a reader assume it means more |
| `post-office` | Post Office (nearest 3) | geography | NearestPoint | LIVE USGS National Map structures layer 38, the fleet's shared post-office source; public domain, 1,799 points in Michigan's envelope with name/address/city/state/ZIP populated on every one. **THIS FETCH PAGES AND EVERY SIBLING'S DOES NOT**, which is the finding worth carrying: the service caps a response at 2,000 records and signals it with HTTP 200 + `exceededTransferLimit`, never an error, so a single enveloped request is safe only by margin. Measured 2026-09-04 in each instance's OWN bbox — post offices il 1,946 · mi 1,799 · ia 1,170 · wi 1,107, fire/EMS **mi 2,838 and il 2,820, both already over the cap**. `il/`'s fire layer was therefore dropping ~820 stations in production, which this row reported and did not fix; **FIXED 2026-09-05** in `il/`'s own change, where the harm was measured before the fix — over a uniform 40x40 grid of Illinois's bbox the truncated set named a different nearest-3 at 58% of points and a different NEAREST station at 27%. The engine's `loadArcGISPaged` could not be reused: it queries `where=1=1` with no geometry, which on a national dataset means fetching the United States | — no officeholder, and none is missing: a post office is a federal facility, not an elected district. **The envelope's out-of-state points are deliberate**: 900 of the 1,799 are in Michigan, the rest Wisconsin 535, Illinois 334 and a handful in IA/OH/IN/MN — for a reader in Menominee the nearest post office really is across the river, and the intro says straight-line distance rather than implying jurisdiction |
| `police-station` | Police Station (nearest 3) | safety | NearestPoint | LIVE USGS National Map structures layer 53 through the same paged envelope loader `post-office` introduced. 1,290 points in Michigan's envelope, all fields populated, measured 2026-09-04 — **under the 2,000-record cap today and paged anyway**, so "is it still under" stops being a fact anyone has to re-check | — no officeholder, and none is missing: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. **IT IS A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION**, and the card's intro says so in the reader's own sentence: which agency answers a 911 call at a point is a service-area question, a separate concept this instance has not been researched for. 608 of the 1,290 are in Michigan; the rest are border-state and deliberately so, since nearest is a proximity fact |
| `fire-station` | Fire & EMS Station (nearest 3) | safety | NearestPoint | LIVE USGS National Map structures layer 51 through the paged envelope loader — **AND THIS IS THE LAYER THAT LOADER EXISTS FOR.** 2,838 points in Michigan's envelope against the service's 2,000-record cap, and the cap is NOT an error: a single request returns HTTP 200 with exactly 2,000 rows and `exceededTransferLimit` set, silently dropping 838 real stations, so a nearest-3 card on the short set would rank the wrong three wherever one of them was closest — looking, at every point, exactly like a correct answer. Paged it is two requests and 2,838, measured 2026-09-04 and asserted in a browser (two requests observed, 2,838 features loaded). **FIRE AND EMS ARE ONE LAYER BECAUSE USGS PUBLISHES THEM AS ONE** ('Fire Stations/EMS Stations'), so the label says both rather than implying a distinction the data does not carry | — no officeholder, and none is missing. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION, the same caveat `police-station` carries: which department or ambulance service is dispatched to a point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for. 1,406 of the 2,838 are in Michigan; the rest are border-state and deliberately so — so the card NAMES EACH STATION'S STATE (added 2026-09-05): border towns share names across the line, and "Menominee, 49858" cannot be told from Menominee, Wisconsin without it |

## Adding or changing a layer — the procedure

1. Consult the matrix first: if a sibling already ships the concept, reuse its recorded
   pattern and source-hunting notes (`docs/EXPANSION_GUIDE.md` §§4.3, 4.6–4.7); if a
   sibling recorded a drop, check whether the rationale applies to your metro before
   re-researching.
2. Build per the guide (`docs/EXPANSION_GUIDE.md` Part 5: worksheet entry → regenerate → registration → source manifest
   → docs), and **in the same change** update: the coverage-map JSON above, the fork's
   inventory table, the concept matrix row (add the row if the concept is new
   fleet-wide), and — if the layer resolves a Parity debt or Backlog entry — move that
   entry accordingly.
1a. **Officeholder sourcing is part of the expansion, not a follow-up** (2026-07 rule,
   `docs/EXPANSION_GUIDE.md` Part 2 rule 4): the change that ships a new
   county's/metro's boundary also determines and BUILDS its officeholder story —
   GIS attrs verified against the published directory where the boundary service
   carries them; otherwise a scraper + builder + weekly PR-opening workflow in the
   same change (bot-managed sites use the requests→Playwright→Internet-Archive engine ladder);
   only when no verifiable source exists does the card fall back to linking the
   official body, with the gap recorded here.
2a. **Card content order (fleet convention):** the result card leads with the layer name
   (card header), then the district identifier, then — wherever a verifiable source
   exists — the representative(s)/officeholder(s), the office location, contact info,
   and a link to more detail, in that order. Deviate only where the concept demands it
   (nearest-N lists, layers with no elected officer) — and when identity/location/contact
   data exists in the layer's source but isn't on the card yet, record the gap in the
   Backlog rather than shipping it silently.
2b. **Card construction (engine-v1.0.10+, docs/CARD_RENDER_API.md):** new and edited
   cards render through the shared card-helpers vocabulary — person rows with
   badges/notes/committee expanders, office groups, nearest rows, link rows, the
   generic field stack — with the district identifier in the header pill
   (`cardIdentifier`), the official link in the footer (`primaryLink`), and name-only
   layers as `compact` cards. The helpers are data-only by contract: never pass HTML
   (`renderFieldList` and the factories' caller-HTML opts are legacy paths kept alive
   only for unmigrated fork call sites, and are scheduled for removal once the
   fleet-wide grep hits zero). The content order in 2a maps onto the vocabulary as:
   pill → person rows → office group → contact line → footer link.
3. If you decide a concept **won't** ship in a metro, add the NO HONEST ANALOG footnote
   with the rationale and source of truth. Silence is the only wrong answer.
4. The weekly fleet-status run cross-checks the coverage map against every fork's live
   worksheet; a mismatch WARNs on the "Fleet status" issue until the guidebook and the
   fleet agree.
